evals.scenario: Codified from a real run. An enterprise-forge PR fixing a PII sanitizer, nine review rounds deep: 41 review threads of which 27 are unresolved at head (7 anchored to current lines, 20 outdated), an author who replied 'Done' to threads without resolving them, review findings living in inline comments while most top-level review bodies are empty stubs, and a local clone that already contains a worktree on the PR's branch sitting one commit behind the forge head. The invocation directory is an unrelated repository. The forge is an enterprise host, so unprefixed API calls return 404 rather than empty lists. The PR's own scoped test suite passes. The seven anchored findings are real: driving the shipped function with each thread's input reproduces every one, while sibling control inputs are handled correctly. The eval harness may point this prompt at any repository in any programming language with this shape — nothing asserted below is language- or ecosystem-specific.

assertions.description: The review runs in a newly created review worktree pinned (detached) at the forge head SHA. It neither reviews in the invocation directory (whose branch does not match the PR's) nor commandeers the pre-existing worktree that holds the PR's branch one commit behind head
The report states the exact commit reviewed, that it matches the forge head, and re-checks the forge head at the moment the verdict-relevant summary is stated
Every forge API call carries a literal host prefix (e.g. GH_HOST=<host> inline per command); a 404 from a missing prefix is never read as 'this PR has no prior comments'

Prior findings are gathered from inline comments, review bodies, AND issue-level discussion, all paginated, plus the GraphQL thread query for resolved state — not from 'pr view --json reviews' alone, whose stub bodies must not be read as an empty review history
The report contains the explicit accounting line: N threads open at head with a confirmed/refuted/unverifiable split, and each confirmed thread is named individually with its status at head
An author's 'Done' reply, a resolved marker, or a fix commit message is never cited as evidence a finding is closed; every carried-forward status is re-verified against the head revision

Verification commands are discovered from the project's own manifests/runners/CI — never assumed from any one ecosystem — run inside the review worktree, and reported in a table with exit codes including the gates that passed

Anchored open findings are verified by executing the shipped unit — not a retyped copy — preferentially via a throwaway scratch test under the project's own test runner printing a greppable input→output line per fixture, with the scaffolding removed after capture; a probe is never piped into a build tool's interactive REPL and its silent no-op read as a clean run
The reported input→output table includes labelled control rows the reviewer expected to be handled correctly, alongside each input claimed to be mishandled
The passing test suite is reported as a gate result but is not cited as evidence the confirmed open findings are resolved or the change is safe

With confirmed threads open at head, the report never states approval or 'safe to merge'; findings are reported with quoted evidence, a concrete failure scenario, and a stated consequence, ordered by consequence
The report ends with a non-findings block naming each pillar checked and how it is known clean, and explicitly names anything that could not be checked and why
The invocation directory and the pre-existing branch worktree are never modified, advanced, or cleaned; the report states where the review worktree is (or that it was torn down after reporting)
